findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (file not found, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or missing file path crashes the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, Error> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| Error::Io(e)) or use ? operator

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on invalid numeric input or if parts has fewer than 2 elements
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV line (missing field or non-numeric value) crashes the program instead of returning a typed parse/field error
findings.fix: Use parts.get(1).ok_or(Error::MissingField) and parse with .map_err(|e| Error::Parse(e)), propagating as Result

findings.problem: Lossy narrowing cast: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value like 70000 wraps to 4464, silently corrupting data without any error or bounds check
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(value).map_err(|_| Error::Overflow) after parsing, or parse directly as u16 with parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err()

findings.problem: Unbounded indexed access parts[0] without bounds check on Vec<String>
findings.failure_mode: Empty or malformed line panics with index-out-of-bounds instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Use parts.first().ok_or(Error::EmptyField) or use split_once(',') to safely extract fields

findings.problem: Unbounded indexed access parts[1] without bounds check on Vec<String>
findings.failure_mode: Line with only one comma-delimited field panics with index-out-of-bounds

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) inside load_sessions mixes logging side effects into data-loading logic
findings.failure_mode: Hidden I/O in the core makes the function non-pure, breaks deterministic testing, and couples domain logic to console output
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely. If logging is needed, push it to a shell layer that calls the pure parsing function and logs results separately

findings.problem: load_sessions bundles I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, logging, and collection into a single function with no clear core/shell split
findings.failure_mode: Cannot test parsing logic in isolation; every test must touch the filesystem or mock std::fs; pure calculation is not separated from side effects
findings.fix: Split into: (1) pure fn parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> and (2) shell fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> that reads, calls parse_record, and handles I/O errors

findings.problem: Per-line allocation: split(',') + map + collect() creates a Vec<String> with owned clones for every line
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded heap allocation per line; unnecessary String clones from .to_string() + .clone() on parts[0]; poor cache locality and alloc pressure
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to get two &str slices, trim them, and construct Record without intermediate Vec or owned Strings. Use split_once for first-delimiter extraction per Holzman rules

findings.problem: parts[0].clone() creates an unnecessary owned String copy when the name is already stored in parts[0] as String
findings.failure_mode: Redundant allocation per record; wasted heap operations on data already owned
findings.fix: Use parts.into_iter().next().unwrap_or_default() or split_once with &str fields to avoid clone entirely

findings.problem: No [dev-dependencies] bench section and no benchmarks/ directory; no performance evidence exists for this crate
findings.failure_mode: Performance regression risk with no baseline; no measured evidence for allocation or throughput claims
findings.fix: Add criterion or similar benchmark framework and measure load_sessions throughput and allocation profile

findings.problem: load_sessions is a hot path (file I/O + parsing) with no profiler or allocation evidence
findings.failure_mode: Unknown performance characteristics; could be silently degrading under load
findings.fix: Add a #[bench] or criterion benchmark measuring bytes parsed per second and allocations per record

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. Seven BLOCKER violations found: two unwrap() calls (lines 9, 19), one lossy as cast (line 19), two unchecked indexings (lines 16, 19), one hidden I/O side effect (line 16), and one architectural split violation (line 8). The code cannot safely handle any malformed input, missing files, or out-of-range values without panicking.
